text:
tara: quick problem note: when upstream model hosts hiccup we tear down and clients immediately hedge. results in duplicate expensive runs. want a short-lived middle state instead of instant teardown.

jin: +1. saw this with the image-infer fleet during snapshotting. a 150ms pause triggers hedging.

omar: what does the middle state do? hold client socket?

tara: not the socket. hold the request context in a tiny local queue on the edge (quarantine) while we probe upstream liveness. client gets a brief deterministic delay or a transparent transient status.

lucy: streaming is tricky. we can't buffer token streams; quarantine only makes sense before any chunk/frame is emitted. need a clear pre-output boundary.

jin: idea: wire header `X-RW-Safepoint: pre-output` or infer from route config (default inference routes = pre-output unless `stream=true`).

omar: and idempotency to avoid billing surprises: `X-RW-Idempotency-Key`. also allow `X-RW-Quarantine-Policy: drop|fallback|hedge`.

tara: probe plan: local HEAD to upstream `/health?probe=quarantine` with jittered backoff (50-150-350ms) up to route window (default 800ms). quarantine must be local to preserve warm caches.

lucy: capacity safety: cap per-instance and per-tenant quarantines (defaults: 20/instance, 200/tenant). emit `quarantine.queue_size` and fire alarm if >80% for 30s.

jin: fallback route optional: route to smaller quantized variant after X ms if probe fails, else hedge to primary. must be opt-in per route.

omar: trace events: `rq.quarantine.start`, `rq.quarantine.probe`, `rq.quarantine.fallback`, `rq.quarantine.abort_client_cancel` so billing can reconcile.

ops-bot: FYI billing flagged duplicate-run spike last week correlated with GC pauses.

tara: next step: I'll draft RFC appendix: state machine (pre-output -> quarantined -> probe -> commit|fallback|abort), headers, defaults, and telemetry labels. cc @jin for route flags, @omar for billing hooks.
